_note: Output formats. sizes = headline / body / small text in px for that canvas, chosen so text reads at the size the platform actually displays the image (a 1600px X image shows at roughly the same width on a phone as a 1080px Instagram post, so it needs ~1.33x the type). Brand rule: two core sizes, small = body minus at most 4px. safe = extra top/bottom space platforms cover with UI (added to the theme's equal margin). crops = centred preview crops a platform applies (lint 'crop'). space = per-format overrides of the theme's rules.space, each with a reason. Sources for every size: platform-sizes.md. layout: stack (header above chart) or side (header column left, chart right); side_col = header column share of the width (default 0.36). notes: false means a stacked canvas is too short to carry notes, so they go only into the caption file; side (landscape) layouts ignore it and set notes in the header column when the space between dek and source holds them.

_note_sizes: Type scale (3 Nov 2026, owner found the proportions off): headline and body on the guide's 8-point scale, small text body minus 4 (the guide's allowance; web minus 2). Headline about 1.5-1.75x body, as the guide asks for headings 'noticeably larger ... but not so large that they overpower' and progressions 'not abrupt'; the old 48/24 pair was 2x, and 28px body sat off the 8-point scale. A story shows at the same width on a phone as a feed post, so it takes the feed scale (40/24/20); 56/32/28 cost dense charts their legibility (3 Nov 2026).

platforms._note: What a default run produces (3 Nov 2026). Each platform names the canvas it uses; output files are output/<theme>/<chart>/<chart>_<platform>_<W>x<H>.png. Several platforms may share one canvas (rendered once, copied). Formats no platform uses (linkedin_landscape, youtube, web, blog) render only with --format=all. Platform canvases render at 1x, so each PNG is exactly the size in its name: Instagram keeps at most 1080px wide and resizes anything larger, and 1600x900 already exceeds a phone's width on X.

instagram-feed.label: Instagram feed and carousel (4:5)
instagram-feed.why: 4:5 is the tallest feed size every account can post; the 3:4 profile grid crop is linted (crops).

instagram-story.label: Instagram story (9:16)
instagram-story.why: Full screen; 250px safe zones top and bottom for Instagram's interface.

youtube-community.label: YouTube Community post (1:1)
youtube-community.why: YouTube recommends square images for Community posts; square fills the mobile feed.

x.label: X / Twitter post (16:9)
x.why: 16:9 at 1600x900 shows uncropped in the timeline on desktop and mobile.

substack-notes.label: Substack Notes (4:5)
substack-notes.why: Substack publishes no Notes spec; Notes are read on phones, so the 4:5 feed image is the default. Check one real Note before relying on it.

blog.label: Blog and Substack posts (1456 wide)
blog.why: Substack's recommended width and post-preview size (1456x1048); reads well in a post body.
